newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile's Colbun stock rises on deal hopes.
newsitem.headline: Chile's Colbun stock rises on deal hopes.

text.p: Chilean state power utility Colbun Machicura's stock climbed at the opening on speculation the government has reached a deal to sell a 37.5 percent stake in the company to a Chilean-Belgian consortium, said dealers.
Colbun, the only large power utility in Chile still in state hands, was up 3.33 percent in early dealing at 46.5 pesos.

State holding agency Corfo is expected to announce at a news conference at 1100 local time/1400 GMT Thursday that it has struck an agreement with a consortium made up of Inversora Electrica Andina and Minera Valparaiso.
Inversora Elctrica Andina is comprised of Belgium's Powerfin SA, Spain's Iberdrola and local company Enagas.
The group was the only one to bid in the sale last week, and its offer was spurned by the government as too low.
But a few days later the government backpedalled and started talks with the consortium.
The state owns 85 percent of Colbun with 15 percent traded on the stock exchange.
